USP 31 (Antivenin (Latrodectus Mactans)). A sterile freeze- dried preparation of specific venom-neutralising globulins ob- tained from the serum of healthy horses immunised against ven- om of black widow spiders (Latrodectus mactans). One dose neutralises the venom in not less than 6000 mouse LD50 of L. mactans. It contains thiomersal as preservative. It should be pre- served in single-dose containers and stored at a temperature not exceeding 40°. Adverse Effects and Precautions As for antisera in general, p.2201. Uses and Administration The use of a spider venom antiserum suitable for the species of spider can prevent symptoms, provided that it is done with the least possible delay; other general supportive measures and symptomatic treatment may also be needed. An antiserum against the black widow spider (Latrodectus mactans) is available in the USA and Canada. The contents of a vial containing at least 6000 antivenin units is the usual dose for adults and children. In severe cases and in children under 12 years of age it is given by intravenous infusion in sodium chlo- ride 0.9% over 15 minutes; in less severe cases, it may be given by intramuscular injection. Antivenoms are also available against other Latrodectus species, including the Australian red-back spider (L. hasselti) and the South African button spiders. An antiserum against the funnel- web spider (Atrax robustus) is available in Australia. Antivenoms have also been developed against Loxosceles spi- ders and against Phoneutria spiders, but there is little evidence of their effectiveness. Spider bites.
